question: In two circles centred at O and O’, the distance between the centres of both circles is 17 cm. The points of contact of a direct common tangent between the circles are P and Q. If the radii of both circles are 7 cm and 15 cm, respectively, then the length of PQ is equal to:
solution:
Given:

The Radii of the two circles are 7 cm and 15 cm

The distance between their centres is 17 cm.

Formula used:

Length of direct common tangent = sqrt {D² - (r₁ - r₂)²} 

Where D = Distance between their centers, r1 = radius of the bigger circle and r2 = radius of the smaller circle

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/726975bbefbb6bc401e04d6b4c972ebcce6acec738379596570646b2b5bc2185.png] 

According to the formula,

Length of PQ = sqrt {17² - (15 - 7)²}

⇒ Length of PQ = sqrt {289 - 64}

⇒ Length of PQ = 15 cm

∴ The length of the direct common tangent is 15 cm.
